description: Intraday. Sells an ATM straddle with 1.5% wings only in the last two calendar days before NIFTY's weekly expiry, after 09:45, while the index is still inside its opening range and VIX is not rising. Intraday because the edge is same-day theta, and wings plus a tight stop cap the worst day.
hypothesis: Near expiry, ATM theta is a large share of the premium within one session. The textbook straddle loses on trend days. Entering only once the first 30 minutes stay inside a range and VIX is flat should skip most trend days and keep the decay. Wings cap gap risk, and the stop is set near the target so costs do not eat the edge. BANKNIFTY's monthly expiry makes it mostly idle, so this is designed for NIFTY. Honest expectation is 1-3% a month, not 5-7%.
lessons: Selling 0-3 DTE premium when IV rank is low and the market is sideways gives no edge: the premium is too cheap to pay for the intraday tail moves. Undefined or loosely defined risk near expiry produces single days of -10% to -20%, which fails the pass rule on its own. Size positions to the actual capital and pick strikes that exist in the chain, or the backtest only describes a few days. A filter on mid IV rank or trend would cut trading to a few times a year, which fails the frequency aim. The next idea needs a hard daily loss cap built in and must enter on most sessions.

The average month was -4.0% (NIFTY) and -2.4% (BANKNIFTY), far from the 5-7% target. Only 36-43% of months were positive. 2024 lost -57% and -47% while holding lost about -6%. edge_t was negative (-1.42, -1.03), so there is no edge at all, not just bad luck. description: Intraday. Sells a near-expiry ATM put spread only after the index trades above its open while VIX falls, and closes it the same day. It is intraday because it needs about 15 decision days a month to pass the 10-trades rule, and because it avoids overnight gaps, which killed every positional seller in the atlas. NIFTY weeklies give the theta; on BANKNIFTY's monthly expiry the edge is mainly skew.
hypothesis: Index puts carry a skew premium: buyers overpay for crash cover. On a day when the index holds above its open and VIX is falling, intraday put demand fades and ATM put IV bleeds, while the drift tends to persist. A defined-risk spread with a stop caps the worst day near 5%. Selling only on confirmed-strength days, not every day, is what sets it apart from the atlas straddles. Honestly this likely earns 1-3% a month, not 5-7%. Reaching 5-7% would need more margin than the -10% worst-day limit allows.
lessons: The core entry loses most in its most common condition: sideways, low IV rank, normal VIX. It is not a filtering problem that one rule change can fix. Single-day losses of 7-9% show the risk per trade is too large for a 30% drawdown limit. Strike selection must be robust on BANKNIFTY (expiry and strike-grid changes) or most sessions are skipped. Positive slices with 3-22 trades should not be chased; that is overfitting.

title: Intraday bull put spread on morning strength with falling VIX

indexes.why_not: lost money on average: -1.14% a month

indexes.warning: skipped on 64% of sessions (147 no strike, 24 no minute data): most days the strategy could not be entered as written, so these numbers describe very few days

why_failed: Both indexes fail. NIFTY loses 1.14% a month on average, is positive in only 43% of months, has a 27.6% fall from its high and a worst day of -9.1%, and edge_t is -0.7, which is no edge. BANKNIFTY loses 3.66% a month, is positive in only 21% of months, falls 42.2% from its high (the limit is 30%), and lags holding in both years. Its edge_t of -2.45 is reliably negative. BANKNIFTY also skipped 64% of sessions (147 'no strike'), so the rules as written cannot be entered on most days. Losses cluster in sideways, low-IV, normal-VIX entries, which is where nearly all trades happen.
why_worked: Very little worked. NIFTY's 2025 beat holding (+12.4% vs +9.0%) but followed a -28% 2024. Entries 4-7 days to expiry were positive on both indexes (NIFTY 22 trades, +0.19% average; BANKNIFTY 11 trades, +2.0% average). NIFTY falling-trend entries were positive (10 trades). description: Intraday. Near expiry, sell an ATM put spread on days the index breaks above its opening range while VIX falls. The intraday mode gives real minute fills, tight stops with no overnight gaps, and the fast theta of the last 3 days. The defined-risk wing keeps margin small enough to open sets in 2025-26.
hypothesis: Index puts carry a skew premium, and on strong mornings with falling VIX that put premium decays fastest near expiry. Requiring breakout plus falling VIX filters out the trend-down days that killed the plain sellers. The wing and a 60% stop cap a bad day near -6%. Honestly, this likely earns 1-3% a month, not 5-7%. It may also trade under 10 times a month on BANKNIFTY, which has only a monthly expiry.
lessons: Taking near-expiry trades whenever IV is low and the market is sideways has a reliably negative edge on both indexes. The edge appears only when premium is rich, and that happens too rarely to reach the trade count needed for 5-7% a month. Filtering down to those few trades would make the version fail on trade frequency. With a significantly negative edge_t after three versions, more tuning is unlikely to help. The next idea should have its edge on ordinary days, should cap daily loss by design (for example defined-risk structures), and should avoid strikes that BANKNIFTY often lacks.

entry.when: dte <= 3 and not event_today and close > or_high and close > day_open and vix_chg_pct < 0 and vix < 22

title: Intraday bull put spread on opening-range breakouts near expiry
why_failed: Both indexes fail the pass rule. NIFTY fell 49.5% from its high (limit 30%), averaged -4.46% a month, was positive in only 14% of months, and had an edge_t of -2.46. That t-value is significantly negative, so the losses are not bad luck. BANKNIFTY's worst day was -11.8% (limit -10%), it fell 31% and averaged -2.36% a month at only 1.1 trades a month, and 26% of its sessions were skipped for having no strike. Holding beat the strategy in every year on both indexes: NIFTY 2025 was -15.6% against +9.0%, BANKNIFTY 2025 -5.9% against +13.5%. Nearly every trade was entered 0-3 days before expiry with IV rank in the low third, and those trades lose about 1.2-2.8% each. The worst days run -6% to -12%, so the losses are large and come in bursts.
why_worked: Very little worked. The few trades entered when VIX was above 18 or IV rank was in the middle third made money (NIFTY 1 trade, BANKNIFTY 2+2). Falling-trend entries on NIFTY were roughly flat. These samples are tiny, so they hint at a direction and prove nothing. They suggest the idea only pays when option prices are rich, and the cheap, low-IV, near-expiry setups make up most of the trades and lose.

description: Intraday. Near expiry (dte <= 3), a weekly option's remaining time value decays sharply within one session, so the theta is worth collecting the same day. Intraday also avoids the overnight gaps that broke the positional sellers. The defined-risk wings keep margin small, so 2025-26 sets can be bought, and they cap the worst minute.
hypothesis: Near expiry, NIFTY weekly premium decays fast inside a day. On days when the index stays inside its 09:15-09:44 range and VIX is not rising, realised movement tends to fall short of implied, so a 20-delta condor kept to the afternoon should earn its decay after costs. The textbook iron fly sat at the money and traded every day; this one avoids trend and vol-spike days. Honestly, 5-7% a month is unlikely: I expect roughly 1-3%. BANKNIFTY's monthly expiry will rarely qualify.
lessons: A high win rate does not survive one uncapped tail day. Each index's failure traces to one or two sessions, so a hard intraday loss cap is the binding constraint. A 0-3 day expiry filter starves BANKNIFTY of trades now that its weekly expiries are gone, and strike lookup fails on most days. That frequency problem is structural and one tweak will not fix it. NIFTY's edge is only noise, and the conditional splits are too thin to filter on without overfitting.

title: Near-expiry inside-range iron condor (NIFTY weekly)

indexes.warning: skipped on 59% of sessions (132 no strike, 24 no minute data): most days the strategy could not be entered as written, so these numbers describe very few days

why_failed: Both indexes fail the worst-day rule: NIFTY -13.9% on 2025-05-12 and BANKNIFTY -11.2% on 2024-10-22 (that same day cost NIFTY -10.4%), so one bad session sinks a month. NIFTY has no real edge. Edge_t is 0.39, only 50% of months are positive and the average is 1.08%, far below 5-7%. Its profit comes from 47 rising-trend or calm/fearful-VIX trades, while the 99 normal-VIX and 98 sideways trades lose money. BANKNIFTY carries a warning: 59% of sessions were skipped (132 no strike), leaving 2.36 trades a month and 33 trades in total. Its 6% average month rests on very few days.
why_worked: The core intraday near-expiry trade has a high win rate (69% NIFTY, 82% BANKNIFTY) and beat holding in every year on both indexes. On BANKNIFTY, the days it could enter were strongly profitable across every VIX and trend bucket. Edge_t is 2.04, so the result is unlikely to be pure luck. Apart from one outlier day, BANKNIFTY's losing days were small: the next worst was -1.96%, and the worst fall was 0.96%.

description: Intraday. Near 14:45, if the index trades above its open, buy an ATM/ATM+2 call debit spread on the nearest expiry and hold it to 15:20. Intraday because the edge is a same-day flow effect and the hard daily cap holds. Defined risk, held for 35 minutes so little time decay, and ATM strikes exist on both indexes.
hypothesis: Research on intraday momentum (Gao et al.; also reported for NSE) finds the day's return so far predicts the last half hour's return, driven by hedging flows and late informed trading. A cheap ATM call spread captures that drift. Risk is defined, capped at 1% of the account, and the hold is too short to bleed much theta. It enters on about 11 up days a month. It is long-only, so down days are idle. The edge per trade is small next to costs, so 1.5-2% a month is unlikely; I expect +0.3-0.8%.
lessons: Before reading the splits, check the win rate. About 1% everywhere means a bug or a structural cost such as spread or stop placement, not an edge to tune. Do not just invert a broken strategy, because that would be fitting to an artifact. Strike selection needs to handle BANKNIFTY's monthly-only expiry. Sizing must cap losses to available capital.

entry.when: close > day_open and close > ema(30) and not event_today

title: Late-day momentum call debit spread (intraday, last 30 minutes)
why_failed: Both indexes fail badly: NIFTY fell 73% from its high and BANKNIFTY 85%, against a 30% limit. Zero months were positive. Win rate is about 1% over 195 trades, and edge_t is -5.6 and -5.4, a strong and consistent negative edge. Every year trailed buy-and-hold. The loss is uniform: about -1.2% to -2.5% per trade in every VIX, trend, expiry and IV split, so no market condition rescues it. A near-zero win rate in every bucket looks mechanical, not like a market effect: possibly a stop inside the spread, a stop hit on the entry bar, or exits priced on the wrong side. BANKNIFTY also skipped 76 sessions for 'no strike' and held 16+ DTE monthlies, so the post-2024 expiry change is handled badly. A -156% year means the sizing or accounting allows losses beyond the capital base.
why_worked: Nothing worked. Trade frequency of about 7 per month is in a usable range, and charges (380-660 rupees per trade) are not the main cause, so the losses come from the entry/exit logic itself.

change_note: Exit-only fix. I removed the premium stop_pct so a quote's spread or the entry bar can no longer trigger a stop, widened the target to 80% of the debit, and use only a 1.5%-of-account loss cap plus a 15:25 close-out. Fill-side and entry-bar checks belong to the engine and cannot be set or verified from YAML. Switch to a new idea if the win rate stays below 20%.
description: Intraday. It buys a near-ATM NIFTY/BANKNIFTY call spread in the last 30 minutes on days that hold above both the open and the opening-range high, and closes by 15:25. Intraday mode keeps the risk to one session, and the defined-risk spread caps each day's loss by design. Entry is unchanged from v1; only the exits change.
hypothesis: Strong days that hold their gains into the close tend to keep drifting up in the final half hour, which index fund and short-covering flows would explain. A debit spread limits the time-decay drag. v1 won 1% of trades, which points to exits firing on the spread or entry noise rather than a real absence of edge. With no premium stop, a wider cap and a 15:25 close, the true edge becomes measurable. I doubt it reaches 1.5-2% a month after two legs of costs on 30-minute holds. If the win rate stays below 20%, abandon the idea.
lessons: Every split loses: every VIX bucket, every trend, every expiry bucket, every IV rank. So this is not a filtering problem; the core entry has negative edge. Win rates of 11-22% with steady small losses suggest a long-premium setup bleeding theta and hitting stops in mostly low-IV, sideways sessions (most trades). Low IV rank dominated and was a poor time for this idea. A strongly negative edge_t on both indexes means this idea should be dropped rather than tuned.

title: Late-day momentum call debit spread v2 (exit mechanics fixed)
why_failed: Version 2 lost heavily on both indexes and is decisively negative, not just unlucky. NIFTY: avg month -5.5%, 7% of months positive, 22% win rate, 55.7% drawdown, edge_t -2.87. BANKNIFTY: avg month -7.0%, 0% of months positive, 11% win rate, 64.4% drawdown, edge_t -3.88. It lost in every year while holding gained (2025: -56% vs +9% NIFTY, -82% vs +13% BANKNIFTY). Losses are consistent near -1 to -2.5% per day, so no single shock caused them. Charges of 25-32k on about 2-4L capital add to the losses. BANKNIFTY skipped 25% of sessions (43 with no strike).
why_worked: Almost nothing worked. The worst single day stayed under 2.6%, so per-trade risk control held. NIFTY trades entered in a rising trend lost least (-0.14% avg) and had the highest win rate (33%). Trade frequency of 5-7 per month is enough for the test.

description: Positional. It rides the index's own upward drift and momentum through a defined-risk call debit spread on the next monthly expiry. Long ITM leg, short OTM leg. Decided at the daily close because the edge is multi-day trend persistence, which needs the 10 years of daily data including 2020. Exits after 10 sessions before expiry, on a trend break, or at a target.
hypothesis: Index momentum is documented and is why Nifty200 Momentum 30 earns about 21% a year. A long-delta call spread taken only in confirmed uptrends turns that drift into leveraged exposure with capped risk. The long 0.65-delta leg is mostly intrinsic and the short 0.30-delta leg collects decay, so net theta is small. Trend exits cut the bleed in falls. I expect about 0.5-1% a month and 2-4 trades a month, so it likely misses the 1.5% target and the frequency rule.
lessons: Three versions of this positional idea have stayed at well under one trade a month with no statistical edge, so it cannot reach 1.5-2% a month. Filters that help one index hurt the other, so condition-slicing is overfitting. A viable idea has to trade often (near-weekly or more, closer to expiry), have a defined maximum loss per trade to cap 5-7% days, and show a positive edge_t on both indexes before fine-tuning.

title: Trend-following ITM-to-OTM bull call debit spread (positional, monthly)

indexes.why_not: lost money on average: -0.04% a month
too slow: 0.2 trades a month (needs 10, or 1.5% a month)

why_failed: Both indexes fail. NIFTY loses on average (-0.04%/month, edge_t -2.77, beats holding in only 1 of 10 years, 31.9% win rate, 21.5% worst fall). BANKNIFTY is slightly positive (+0.23%/month) but trades only 0.24 times a month, never beats holding in any year, and edge_t is -1.73. Trade frequency (0.4 and 0.24 per month) is far below the 10 needed, so most months sit flat (median 0%, only 18-23% of months positive). Entries made only at 16+ days to expiry with long ~10-day holds leave the strategy mostly idle. Single-day losses of 7% show uncapped risk on the trades it does take.
why_worked: Very little. BANKNIFTY trades entered in calm VIX (<13) and rising trend were profitable (6 trades, +4.1% average), and NIFTY sideways-trend entries were mildly positive. But the samples are tiny, the two indexes disagree (rising trend is the worst bucket on NIFTY and the best on BANKNIFTY), and the edge test is negative on both. These look like noise, not a repeatable edge.

description: Intraday. Entries on most sessions after a narrow first 30 minutes, closed by 15:15. Intraday keeps each loss to about one capped day, with no overnight gap. Defined 1% wings and a 1.5% account cap keep the worst day far inside -10%. It needs the weekly NIFTY expiry. BANKNIFTY's monthly option decays little in a day, so BANKNIFTY is expected to be weak.
hypothesis: A narrow 09:15-09:44 range and VIX not rising mean realized volatility is clustering low. The 09:45 ATM straddle still prices the full day's expected move, so selling it then captures implied-over-realized premium on ordinary days, not only rare high-IV days. Wings and the cap cut off the tail days that broke earlier sellers. The edge is likely thin after four legs of spread and charges. I doubt it reaches 1.5-2% a month; +0.5-1% on NIFTY is the realistic hope, and the t of 2 is the risk.
lessons: A strongly negative edge_t on both indexes means the core entry logic is wrong, not the parameters. The losses are large single-day blowups (-23% to -27%), which points to missing per-trade loss caps and over-sized positions relative to capital. Low IV rank and calm VIX entries lost consistently, so this setup should not trade in low-volatility regimes. Strike selection fails often on BANKNIFTY, and charges are a large drag at this trade frequency. Further tweaks to this idea are not worth the last version.

It lost in both years (-24.6% vs holding -6.8%; -74.9% vs +9%). BANKNIFTY: win rate 7.7%, worst day -27.3%, drawdown 71%, edge_t -2.96, and 2025 at -109.8% vs holding +13.5%. It traded under once a month, and 36.6% of sessions were skipped (60 had no strike). Every split lost money. Charges of about 50-58k on fewer than 30 trades ate a large share of capital. description: Intraday. Sells an ATM straddle on the nearest expiry after the opening range has formed (10:15-11:00), with wings 1.5% out so risk is defined on both indexes. It closes by 15:10, and a 1.2% account loss cap fixes the worst day by design. It trades on most sessions, so the trade-count rule can be met.
hypothesis: Indian index options price a high, front-loaded intraday volatility. Once the 09:15-09:44 range is set and price is back inside it, realized volatility usually falls into midday while ATM premium still carries morning fear. Selling that premium, with wings set as a % of the index so strikes exist on both NIFTY and BANKNIFTY, may earn a small edge after costs on ordinary days, and the cap stops one-day tails. I doubt it reaches 1.5-2% a month; a realistic hope is 0.5-1% with a passing worst day and drawdown, and the luck test is the likely failure.
lessons: A 3-5% win rate with losses in every regime means the entry has no edge, probably buying premium that decays intraday. Charges (62.9k and 83.1k) were large next to the capital. Skip counts above 100% of sessions mean position size is far beyond the account. The next idea should fit the capital first and should not depend on intraday long premium. I could not compare with earlier versions because their results were not in this input.
